title: Annotatio VI §.IV: Ad Inquis. Januarii — sacrament stands for body/blood; figure → proper
pass_a_gloss: To Januarius’s Inquiries, after he had spoken in that manner, it clearly appears that when the disciples first received the Lord’s body and blood they did not receive fasting — a little later, in place of the Lord’s body and blood he puts Sacrament: for neither, he says, because the Lord gave after meals should brethren therefore come breakfasted or suppered to receive that Sacrament. Behold the metonymy explained, and the figured speech reduced to proper locution, pp. 181–182.
pass_b_english: In Ad Inquis. Januarii he says the disciples first received “body and blood” not fasting — then swaps in “sacrament”: they need not come already fed to that sacrament.
So the figure is reduced to proper speech (pp. 181–182).
source_text: Ad inquis. Januar. ad eum modum cum dixisset, liquido apparet quum primùm acceperunt discipuli corpus & sanguinem Domini, non eos accepisse jejunos, paulo post, loco corporis & sanguinis Domini ponit Sacramentum: neque enim, inquit, quia post cibos dedit Dominus, propterea pransi aut cænati, fratres ad illud Sacramentum accipiendum, venire debent. En metonymiam explicatam, figuratámque, in propriam reductam locutionem pag. 181. & 182.
